unit: One authenticated tenant VM incarnation encloses many untrusted actors; each actor retains private sealed memory and mailbox ownership
trustModel: Host authenticates tenant and actor execution; guest code never receives a tenant handle, root VM, raw mutable heap pointer, or actor ticket as ambient authority

requirements.tenant: Tenant identity consists of canonical ID, generation and opaque host-local authorization; no tenant lookup by guest-supplied string
requirements.actor: Actor capability requires exact tenant incarnation and exact current actor incarnation; same ID or epoch from another root is never authority
requirements.memory: Private actor relative heap plus bounded tenant aggregate; no borrowed references or shared mutable buffers cross actor or tenant domains
requirements.messaging: Authenticated actor turn, bounded owned-copy mailboxes, aggregate tenant and host quotas; cross-tenant transport requires a distinct trusted serialization broker
requirements.lifecycle: Quiescence must fence spawn, message and turn admission before drain; stale references and borrowed execution views never resurrect actors
requirements.kill: Tenant termination revokes all actor grants and clears queues but full backend physical guest preemption and resource-loan retirement remain mandatory separate acceptance gates
requirements.scheduling: Different actors in one tenant may make progress independently; same actor turns may not overlap; per-tenant fairness across the process root must be proven in the real scheduler
